answer: The quartz cap is enforced at intake and kernel reveals the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, as each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a canyon tag. That is 34 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
